batch_strategy: Use 32 distinct supplied candidate IDs to test local solvent-response curves, endpoint-specific loading effects, and transfer across chemically related retention regimes. Freeze the supplied V1/V2 point predictions in each reason.

choices.reason: m209, 20/1, 50 uL: tests loading sensitivity at the composition where the latest 100 uL measurement substantially exceeded its acquisition-time V2 prediction. This distinguishes a persistent phenolic completion tail from a loading-specific effect. Frozen V1/V2: 21.42722511291504/55.12896728515625 mL.

m209, 50/1, 150 uL: extends the phenolic trifluoromethyl ether response beyond its measured 20/1 tail. Together with the lower-loading 20/1 selection, it tests continued growth versus saturation without assuming that a large predicted tail will occur. Frozen V1/V2: 30.401643753051758/76.38951873779297 mL.

m11 acetophenone oxime, 5/1, 100 uL: fills the loading-matched gap between measured 2/1 and 10/1 conditions after recent V2 overprediction at 2/1. This locates the beginning of the oxime's stronger retention response. Frozen V1/V2: 6.786659240722656/20.542381286621094 mL.

m11, 20/1, 100 uL: complements the selected 5/1 point and measured 10/1 and 50/1 anchors at the same loading. It tests whether V2 expands gradually or sharply before the very broad measured 50/1 interval. Frozen V1/V2: 20.20538330078125/47.40135192871094 mL.

m130 dimethylbenzonitrile, 5/1, 50 uL: adds an intermediate solvent condition to a scaffold whose historical extreme weak-eluent prediction proved incorrect. It tests local response shape instead of transferring a generic nitrile tail. Frozen V1/V2: 4.775690078735352/12.930675506591797 mL.

m130, 20/1, 50 uL: pairs with the selected 5/1 point to map composition response at fixed loading. Existing 50/1 measurements are ordinary relative to amino-nitrile tails, making this an informative test of structural-context transfer. Frozen V1/V2: 6.823349952697754/13.317602157592773 mL.

m130, 20/1, 150 uL: forms a controlled loading contrast with the selected 50 uL experiment. The predictor is almost insensitive to this change; the labels can establish whether that flat response is appropriate for this nitrile. Frozen V1/V2: 6.731076240539551/13.389365196228027 mL.

m45 2-bromopropionic acid, 10/1, 100 uL: brackets the measured positive 5/1 and 20/1 responses at fixed loading. This constrains interpolation near a scaffold with a nonphysical recorded 50/1 endpoint pair. Frozen V1/V2: 20.044740676879883/40.48536682128906 mL.

m45, 20/1, 50 uL: adds the missing low-loading endpoint alongside measured 100 and 150 uL conditions. It tests acid loading dependence and helps distinguish the ordinary positive response branch from the isolated 50/1 anomaly. Frozen V1/V2: 26.05245018005371/55.79969787597656 mL.

m204 3-phenylpropanol, 1/1, 50 uL: establishes the low-loading start of a two-point solvent-response experiment. Existing stronger-eluent measurements are ordinary, whereas weaker-eluent conditions give much later retention. Frozen V1/V2: 8.857678413391113/16.630842208862305 mL.

m204, 2/1, 50 uL: changes only PE/EA relative to the selected 1/1 point and complements measured 2/1 at 100 uL. This separates low-loading solvent response from the large alcohol-family corrections seen at weaker eluent. Frozen V1/V2: 13.315810203552246/21.808202743530273 mL.

m119 methoxyphenethyl alcohol, 1/1, 50 uL: completes the low end of the measured 1/1 loading series. Its label helps determine whether the large correction observed at 5/1 transfers to strong eluent or remains localized. Frozen V1/V2: 12.802560806274414/20.551334381103516 mL.

m135 methylbenzyl alcohol, 5/1, 150 uL: completes a loading series whose measured low and middle loads shift V1 more than V2. It tests whether the model can learn endpoint-specific loading effects across aromatic alcohols. Frozen V1/V2: 22.415088653564453/35.35677719116211 mL.

m114 methoxybenzophenone, 10/1, 50 uL: with the selected 20/1, 100 uL point, fills the opposite corners of a composition-by-loading comparison supported by existing 10/1, 100 uL and 20/1, 50 uL measurements. Frozen V1/V2: 8.462737083435059/23.622657775878906 mL.

m114, 20/1, 100 uL: completes the paired comparison with the selected 10/1, 50 uL experiment. These labels distinguish solvent response from loading response in a neutral ketone/ether environment with measured late weak-eluent behavior. Frozen V1/V2: 17.20966339111328/36.93690490722656 mL.

m98 naphthylacetate ester, 10/1, 50 uL: begins a loading-matched 10/1-to-50/1 solvent contrast. Existing middle-loading measurements provide additional references, so the pair can teach both response curvature and loading transfer. Frozen V1/V2: 11.75296401977539/21.37531089782715 mL.

m98, 50/1, 50 uL: pairs with the selected 10/1 experiment and the measured 50/1, 100 uL anchor. This tests whether the predictor's nearly flat loading response preserves both endpoints in an aromatic ester. Frozen V1/V2: 27.216487884521484/49.57878875732422 mL.

m190 bromosalicylaldehyde, 20/1, 100 uL: fills a weak-eluent gap between measured conditions and tests a phenolic aldehyde response distinct from m209. The selected positional analogue provides a useful comparison, although recorded loading conditions differ. Frozen V1/V2: 10.896905899047852/28.532014846801758 mL.

m186 bromosalicylaldehyde, 20/1, 100 uL: complements the selected m190 point and its own measured 50/1 anchors. It tests whether positional environment and recorded loading conditions lead to different onset and completion responses despite similar functional groups. Frozen V1/V2: 9.170552253723145/25.4979248046875 mL.

m104 methyl anthranilate, 20/1, 150 uL: adds a new loading point near repeated middle-loading measurements with different completion endpoints. It can establish whether higher loading produces a consistent continuation, while recognizing unresolved variation at identical recorded inputs. Frozen V1/V2: 11.432847023010254/18.041528701782227 mL.

m86 ethyl para-aminobenzoate, 2/1, 50 uL: supplies a low-loading counterpart to the measured 100 uL condition. It tests transfer of amine/ester loading effects before the much later measured 5/1 response. Frozen V1/V2: 12.80916976928711/25.65180015563965 mL.

m92 methyl phenylglyoxylate, 5/1, 50 uL, loaded in EA: complements measured 5/1 at 150 uL and the substantial loading dependence observed at 2/1. The model predicts little loading sensitivity here, providing a direct test. Frozen V1/V2: 7.996985912322998/26.599943161010742 mL.

m92, 20/1, 150 uL, loaded in EA: extends the loading comparison into weaker mobile phase alongside measured 20/1 middle-loading anchors. It tests whether completion-volume loading effects persist across composition rather than treating EA loading solvent as mobile-phase composition. Frozen V1/V2: 12.607661247253418/31.405799865722656 mL.

m82 ethyl acetoacetate, 10/1, 50 uL: tests the low-loading counterpart to recent 150 uL outcomes with late completion. This can determine whether the latest V2 correction transfers across loading or conceals a loading-dependent interval change. Frozen V1/V2: 18.600444793701172/45.188682556152344 mL.

m123 para-dimethoxybenzene, 5/1, 100 uL: begins a matched comparison where the model predicts later endpoints than at 10/1. Measuring both compositions tests whether this inversion is an interpolation artifact or an empirical local feature. Frozen V1/V2: 9.005475997924805/17.007177352905273 mL.

m123, 10/1, 100 uL: holds loading conditions fixed relative to the selected 5/1 point. Existing 2/1 and 20/1 anchors make the predicted intervening decrease particularly informative for learning neutral aromatic ether solvent response. Frozen V1/V2: 6.358797073364258/12.809115409851074 mL.

m27 chlorinated aliphatic ketone, 0/1, 100 uL: supplies a strong-eluent endpoint for a matched solvent comparison. The model predicts greater retention here than at 10/1, a testable pattern that should not be rejected solely from normal-phase priors. Frozen V1/V2: 6.341184139251709/10.513263702392578 mL.

m27, 10/1, 100 uL: pairs with the selected pure-EA point at identical loading. Existing 2/1 and 50/1 measurements make this useful for distinguishing a real decreasing response region from model interpolation failure. Frozen V1/V2: 5.153517723083496/6.707408428192139 mL.

m208 para-iodophenol, 5/1, 100 uL: adds the middle-loading point alongside measured 5/1 at 150 uL and a broader weak-eluent curve. It tests whether phenolic retention corrections generalize across substitution and loading. Frozen V1/V2: 9.66954517364502/16.481285095214844 mL.

m87 ethyl methoxybenzoate, 50/1, 100 uL: extends the latest 20/1 middle-loading observation and complements a measured low-loading 50/1 anchor. This checks neutral ester/ether transfer alongside the selected amino-esters. Frozen V1/V2: 26.36104393005371/50.98093032836914 mL.

m88 ethyl meta-aminobenzoate, 1/1, 50 uL: fills the strong-eluent gap between measured pure-EA and 2/1 conditions on this scaffold. It improves transfer among amino-benzoate environments without attributing all differences to substitution position alone. Frozen V1/V2: 7.030359745025635/13.452075004577637 mL.

m211 phenylpyridine, 20/1, 50 uL: combines with measured low-loading 10/1 and middle-loading 20/1 anchors to constrain solvent and loading response in a basic heteroaromatic environment. This extends the batch's learning beyond oxygen-containing scaffolds. Frozen V1/V2: 27.69409942626953/53.960418701171875 mL.

hypotheses.content: Hydrogen-bonding aromatic compounds have scaffold-specific weak-eluent completion responses. Phenols and oximes should not share a uniform V2 correction or a common tail-growth rule.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These observations include ordinary completion, moderate intervals, and very late V2 values within related donor-containing chemistry. Local labels can teach which structural environments and compositions require separate endpoint responses.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m209 retain its late completion at lower loading and continue growing at 50/1, and do the oxime and substituted phenols follow different transition shapes?

hypotheses.content: Loading dependence can affect V1 and V2 differently and can change with solvent composition. Nearly flat predicted loading responses may miss these effects, although variation between repeated recorded conditions limits causal interpretation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The predictor needs endpoint-specific structure-by-loading and composition-by-loading relationships. Completing local contrasts is more informative than collecting many unrelated loading points.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected loading contrasts preserve V2 while shifting V1, expand completion at nearly fixed onset, or remain flat as currently predicted?

hypotheses.content: A nitrile group alone does not determine weak-eluent retention: dimethylbenzonitrile should not inherit amino-nitrile or cyano-benzophenone tails without condition-specific evidence.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This family contains historical errors in both directions. A local dimethylbenzonitrile curve can constrain inappropriate transfer from more strongly interacting nitrile-containing environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the unmeasured 5/1 and 20/1 dimethylbenzonitrile responses modest at both loading levels, or is there a localized response missed by its measured endpoints?

hypotheses.content: The m45 acid response at 10/1 is likely to remain on the positive retention branch bracketed by measured 5/1 and 20/1 conditions, despite its nonphysical recorded 50/1 endpoint pair.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: New neighboring labels may constrain how an anomalous observation influences interpolation. The recorded anomaly is evidence of an unresolved data issue or missing information, not an established chemical response mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the loading-matched 10/1 experiment interpolate between the positive 5/1 and 20/1 endpoints, and does low loading at 20/1 support the same branch?

hypotheses.content: The predicted retention decreases from 5/1 to 10/1 for m123 and from 0/1 to 10/1 for m27 may reflect interpolation artifacts. Matched-loading measurements can distinguish those artifacts from empirical nonmonotonic responses.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Resolving these inversions can improve solvent-response interpolation for common neutral compounds. Normal-phase solvent-strength expectations motivate the test but do not establish that the predictions are wrong.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the measured endpoint orderings reproduce the predicted decreases when all recorded loading conditions are held fixed?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes reinforce endpoint-specific reasoning. The phenolic trifluoromethyl ether and ethyl acetoacetate still showed underestimated completion volumes, while the oxime, dimethylbenzophenone, and indene showed V2 overprediction. Several simple halogenated aromatics were already predicted closely. I therefore shifted from broad chemical coverage toward local composition and loading contrasts around these transferable failure patterns. Historical extreme predictions are not treated as current residuals, and repeated-input variation is not assigned a mechanism without evidence.
batch_rationale: All 32 choices are distinct supplied candidate IDs, with no repeated molecule-condition tuple within this batch and no pending experiments to duplicate. The batch combines matched solvent contrasts for m204, m130, m98, m123, m27, and m11 with loading comparisons supported by existing observations. The m114 selections complete a small composition-by-loading comparison; m92, m82, m135, and the amino-esters test endpoint-specific loading transfer. Phenols and the acid probe localized weak-eluent behavior, while neutral ester/ether and basic heteroaromatic anchors provide useful structural comparisons. Quantile widths are secondary evidence from one predictor, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty; elution interval width is treated as a measured response feature. These labels should help retraining learn conditional response shape and reduce both excessive tail extrapolation and missed late completion across the Row-distribution.
